messages:
Sam: heads up — during the 02:10 UTC pager we saw a noisy combination of slow p99s and transient 503s. I'm opening this thread to capture what we want in a post-incident Grafana dashboard so we can run a proper alert-tuning pass and make the on-call handoff cleaner next time.

Anya: thanks. quick context: impact window ~02:06–02:23 UTC. customer-facing error rate peaked ~2.8% for /v1/generate, p99 latency for long prompts jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.9s. No data lost. Some Dedicated customers saw request queuing and retries.

Derek: incident-bot summary (copied):
incident-bot: PAGERS: 2 alerts fired: `service.p99_latency_v1` (threshold >1.5s) oncall=SRE-1, and `ingress.503_rate` (threshold >1%) oncall=SRE-1. Auto-escalation ran at +10m.

Oliver: from the live mitigation notes — we briefly flipped routing policy to route to the fallback model variant at 02:12 to restore tail latency. That reduced errors but increased cost. For the dashboard we'd like a panel that shows routing decisions over time (which model variant handled x% of traffic).

Emily: proposed golden signals for the dashboard:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 by API route and model family
- Errors: 4xx/5xx rates, request-drop rate, retried requests
- Saturation: GPU utilization, queue depth, connection count
- Traffic: RPS, average tokens per request, burstiness (1m/5m/1h)

Sam: agreed. also add: KV/prefix cache hit rate and hot-shard counts. Cache misses amplified load during the spike.

Derek: we need drilldowns per-customer for Dedicated customers. Add a dropdown variable for `customer_id` so on-call can quickly check if an SLA-bound tenant was impacted. Also a `region` variable.

Anya: alert tuning follow-ups from the incident:
- `service.p99_latency_v1` threshold triggered too early on normal load spikes. Proposal: change threshold to 1.7s and add `for: 120s` (so flapping <2min ignored).
- `ingress.503_rate`: keep threshold at 1% but add suppression when routing to fallback is active (otherwise we get duplicate pages).

Kevin: +1 on hysteresis. Also suggest converting `ingress.503_rate` alert to check both absolute rate and relative increase: fire only when 503_rate > 0.01 AND 503_rate / baseline_1h > 1.5. That should reduce noisier false positives during rollout spikes.

Oliver: UI notes for panels:
1) Overview row: RPS, p99, error rate, GPU avg util (single-line sparkline)
2) Golden signals row: stacked p50/p95/p99 time series with shadings
3) Drilldown row: per-route p99 heatmap, per-customer error table
4) Routing row: model-variant split stacked area chart + fallback toggles
5) Resource row: GPU queue depth, memory pressure, autoscaler events
6) Audit row: recent deploys / canaries overlay (deploy-bot events)

Sam: can we also add an interactive timeline (event markers) that shows when alerts fired, when mitigation (fallback routing) was enabled, and when the on-call handoff occurred? That helped during the postmortem.

Emily: yes — Grafana supports event markers; we can push annotated events via our alert webhook. I'll draft the event payload we need. Example:```json
{
  "title": "fallback enabled",
  "time": 1670000000000,
  "tags": ["mitigation","routing"],
  "text": "Routing switched to fallback-model-v2 due to p99 spike"
}
```
(we'll translate timestamps).

Derek: panel-level alerts — for the retro dashboard we should not fire paging alerts from the dashboard itself. Instead, embed rules links that point to thealert repo. The dashboard should be read-only for oncall except a small playbook button that expands next steps.

Sam: handoff capture — when SRE-1 paged SRE-2 at 02:20 UTC, SRE-2 confirmed handoff at 02:22 and monitored until 02:30 when errors normalized. Please add that note as an entry in the timeline.

incident-bot: incident-bot: reminder — please file a follow-up ticket for alert-rule changes. Use label `alert-tuning` and link the dashboard PR.

Anya: next steps / owners:
- Emily: prototype dashboard and push to `grafana/prod/dashboards/` as `oncall-pulseboard-v1` (ETA 48h)
- Kevin: write alert-rule proposals (PR against `alerts/`), include thresholds and hysteresis examples (ETA 24h)
- Derek: add `customer_id` variable mapping and a sample per-customer panel (ETA 48h)
- Sam: coordinate with product for customer-impact note and send to CS (ETA 12h)

Kevin: I'll also run a small canary of the new alert thresholds in the dev cluster for 24h and capture false positives. Will report back.

Oliver: for the panel implementations, suggestion for panel queries:
- p99 latency by route: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model))`
- fallback routing split: `sum(rate(routing_variant_count[1m])) by (variant)`

Emily: I'll add links in the dashboard to the runbook and to the incident timeline. Also will include a compact table of affected customers with columns: customer_id, tenant_type, peak_error_rate, peak_p99, notes.

Sam: nice. let's keep this focused — we want the dashboard to help on-call triage (fast root-cause signals), not to be a full observability playbook. If owners agree, go ahead and create the PRs and mention this thread.

Anya: noted. tagging: @Emily @Kevin @Derek — pls update this thread with PR links when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
